title: What Your Body Can Regrow, Ranked
sources: Liver: Cleveland Clinic / NIH (Michalopoulos 2007, J Cell Physiol): after up to two-thirds of the liver is removed, it regrows to its original mass within weeks to a few months
Bone: NHS / AAOS OrthoInfo: most broken bones heal in about six to eight weeks
Skin: the epidermis renews itself roughly every four to eight weeks (Cleveland Clinic; Hoath & Leahy 2003)
Stomach lining: surface cells of the stomach lining are replaced every few days (about 3-5 days), constantly worn by acid (Cell Biology by the Numbers; Karam 1999)
Cornea: most corneal abrasions heal within one to three days (American Academy of Ophthalmology)
Tooth enamel: enamel has no living cells, so the body cannot regrow it once lost (NIDCR / American Dental Association)
